Usage: rhythm-sightread allow <eco:name@version>... --reason <text> | --from <report.json> | list | remove <ref> | import <file>

Records that someone reviewed a version, so later reviews show its findings as
allowed. An entry is bound to the sha256 of the archive that was verified: allow
fetches and verifies the version itself, or takes the hash from a saved report
with --from. It refuses a version that couldn't be verified or doesn't match its
published hash. list prints the entries, remove drops one and import merges
another allowed.yaml. Commit the file and protect it with CODEOWNERS.

Flags:
  --by <name>       the name of who reviewed it (default git config user.name,
                    else $USER)
  --config <file>   read this config file instead of the nearest
                    .sightread/config.yaml
  --file <file>     the allow file (default .sightread/allowed.yaml next to the
                    config)
  --force           replace an entry that allows the same version with another
                    sha256
  --from <report>   take every update of this saved JSON report
  --json            allow list: print the kind allowed JSON document
  --no-config       read no config
  --offline         use only cached archives (also RHYTHM_OFFLINE)
  --reason <text>   why it is accepted, in text the next person understands
                    (required when adding)
  --signals <IDs>   only these signal IDs (default every finding of that
                    version)
  --until <date>    date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which the entry no longer counts

Examples:
  rhythm-sightread allow npm:sharp@0.33.5 --reason "known install script" --signals npm-install-script-new
  rhythm-sightread allow --from review.json --reason "reviewed in PR 412"
  rhythm-sightread allow list --json
  rhythm-sightread allow remove npm:sharp@0.33.5
  rhythm-sightread allow import ~/agency/allowed.yaml
